summary: Round 22 recheck, 28 Sep 01:00-01:25Z. At 00:56Z probes 47-49 were PENDING and our best was exp70g at 0.956. About 60 items rechecked in rounds 2-21 were skipped, including the whole insertion-volume family, the DC family, secondary swaps, CI/localisation (R18), node count and E10 thresholds. I picked three closures that no earlier round had re-read. (A) I-046, Eric's sub-voxel refinement (lab +0.0078, LB -0.002 twice). The closure of the lever stands. But R18 promoted it to the 'nearest transfer record' for coordinject, and the finals CI caveat (READ TABLE v2 (9)) still quotes it that way, which is wrong. Eric's change was a heuristic, peak-level refinement with an undisclosed method, made on the pre-head 0.947 stack. It most likely fed the linking gates and so changed topology. Coordinject is a post-CSV integer shift that leaves topology byte-identical (the exp79a dummy has the same nodes, forks and edges as exp70g). There is no like-for-like record, and probe 48 will be the first. Fix the caveat text; the probe-48 codes do not change. (B) The division candidate-supply family: I-080 (wider second-daughter gate), I-059 (B32), I-060 (B35) and I-064 (DaughterNet-B). The closures STAND, now measured on x138 (exp60 lab, 56 clips, 99 GT divisions). The insertion's in-gate supply above threshold is used up by cap 24 fc2. Division TP/FP: cap6 25/35, cap12fc2 28/42, cap24fc2 30/47, cap48fc2 30/51, uncapped 30/59. The GT divisions still missed split into: claimed daughter 32, one daughter undetected 21, orphan daughter scored < 0.4 11, outside the geometry gates 5, parent side 4. So a wider gate reaches at most 5 of 99. In 34 of 35 claimed cases the claimant is unmatched, so fixing one is +1 TP edge, -1 FP edge and +1 division TP. But DaughterNet scores only 3 of 35 at >= 0.4, and the relaxed-steal pool holds 2.9M triples. The next lever is a theft-aware ranker, post-deadline. (C) I-082, Corwin's MITO3 GBM division ADD. Both recorded reasons are partly wrong. The number is a 199-film out-of-fold figure, not an in-sample one. MITO3 needs no MITOSE head: it is a post-CSV, edges-only, never-raise stage run from mito3_ship.py plus a public CC0 LightGBM booster (s1_NK_ship89_plus_collision_deployed.txt, 520,226 B, listed at 01:1xZ). It also targets exactly the claimed-daughter pool that (B) finds our ranker misses. It is still NOT a 28-29 Sep item: it is new code after R8, has no honest lab (the deployed booster is presumably fit on all train films), its runtime is unmeasured, and at top-k 1 per film its OOF volume is +2 TP / +2 FP on 199 films. It goes to the head of the post-deadline division-ADD list. Nothing was submitted, pushed or committed. The finals stay {#37, #38} until the user re-ticks on 29 Sep.

findings.what: I-046 is Eric's probability-weighted / sub-voxel peak refinement (Corwin also ships k10_subvox). OLD VERDICT: refuted, 'lever closed in practice'. Evidence: Eric reported '+0.0078 on 12 official val videos with divisions, -0.002 on the LB, twice' (v3 s_merge assumptions; discussion 742064). Round 18's skeptic then made it the 'nearest transfer record' for coordinject, and it entered the CI caveat of READ TABLE v2 (9) and the finals card: 'nearest transfer record: Eric sub-voxel lab +0.0078 -> LB -0.002'. WHAT CHANGED: coordinject (CI) is now on the board as probe 48 (exp79a = exp70g + CI, ref 56623105). Its dummies show that CI is a post-CSV integer shift that leaves topology byte-identical: exp79a has 121,252 nodes, 81 forks and 117,083 edges, exactly exp70g's; 91.5% of rows moved, by a median 0.51-0.69 um. Eric's change differs in four ways. (1) It was made on the 0.947 stack, before any learned head, when the grid error was ~1.69 um against 1.53 um after V1284. (2) It was a PEAK-level refinement, so the moved coordinates fed the ILP, relink, gap and division gates that were tuned on grid coordinates, and topology most likely changed. His -0.002 therefore bundles linking changes that CI cannot make. (3) The method was never disclosed ('a sub-voxel peak refinement'), so there is nothing to compare mechanism by mechanism. (4) His 12 videos were in-sample for detectors trained on all 199, which is the same caveat our CI lab has, and it cannot tell the two apart. NEW VERDICT: the I-046 closure stands (we have no such lever and none is proposed). Its use as CI's transfer record is WRONG: it is a same-sign anecdote from a different class, not a calibration. No like-for-like record exists. The 4-clip in-sample CI lab shows its sign flipping with alpha (a0.3 -0.00125, a0.5 +0.00215, a1.0 -0.005; R18 check_coord_refiner.json), so on an unseen embryo the sign is simply unknown. Probe 48's display against exp70g 0.956, gated by the R21-A3 (b) CI-RAN rule, will be the first real record. Consequence: the probe-48 codes and W2b rows do not change. Only the caveat text and the private prior's reasoning change. The private prior stays 'unknown to slightly negative' because the refiner was trained on train embryos, not because of Eric.

findings.what: Division candidate-supply family: I-080, the asymmetric/wider second-daughter gate ('radius 30 um adds 1 of 151; losses are detection + claimed daughters', measured on pre-x138 graphs); I-059, the B32 pair model ('orphan pool reaches 58/151; detection ceiling 121/151'); I-060, the B35 second detector pass ('151/151 at +24% candidate nodes'); and I-064, DaughterNet-B ('needs >= 45% insertion precision'). WHAT CHANGED: division ADD volume moves the public board (probe 45: cap 6 = 0.956), and the insertion now steals. Either could have changed which pool is binding. MEASURED on x138 (exp60 lab, 56 clips, 99 GT divisions, official metric; control parity 16/25/83 and ins35 25/31/74 match results.md). Division TP/FP: cap6 25/35, cap12fc2 28/42, cap24fc2 30/47, cap48fc2 30/51, uncapped 30/59. The 11 in-gate orphan daughters that score >= 0.4 in the control are all consumed by cap 24 fc2 (5 left under cap 4/6). The GT divisions still missed at cap24fc2 are: CLAIMED daughter 32 (29 outside the insertion's steal gates, 3 in the gates but scored < 0.4); ONE DAUGHTER UNDETECTED 21; ORPHAN DAUGHTER scored < 0.4 11; orphan outside the geometry gates 5; parent missing/unlinked/linked elsewhere 4. Claimed cases in the control (35): the claimant is unmatched in 34/35, so the claiming edge is an evaluable FP and a correct fix is worth +1 TP edge, -1 FP edge and +1 division TP. 32/35 claiming edges are motion_relinked, and edge_prob is >= 0.6 on 19 of them. With steal_prob_max relaxed, 25/35 pass the geometry, but DaughterNet scores only 3/35 at >= 0.4, and the relaxed-steal pool holds 2,894,751 triples (base rate ~1e-5). NEW VERDICT: UPHELD, with sharper reasons. A wider gate (I-080) can reach at most the 5 out-of-gate orphans. B32 and B35 attack the 21 undetected daughters, but at a candidate-node cost that has not changed. DaughterNet-B's 45% bar was set on the old public break-even, and the cap-6 flip shows the public pays more per fork than the lab, so that bar was too high. The item still needs training, so it stays post-deadline. The next division lever after the caps is a THEFT-AWARE ranker over motion-relinked claimants, which is where the largest remaining pool sits. Caveat: this is an in-sample lab, and the cap-6 flip shows it under-values forks on the public embryo. The supply COUNTS are structural, but their public worth is not.

findings.what: I-082 is Corwin's MITO3 GBM division ADD stage (team Corwin, public 0.965). OLD VERDICT: refuted, 'Trained on train GT (in-sample) and tiny' (FINAL_REPORT_v4 section 2). Curation 12 added 'cannot plug into x138: the 10 MITOSE head checkpoints are not public; our DaughterNet insertion fills the role'. No round from 2 to 21 re-checked it. WHAT CHANGED: (1) division ADDs pay more on public than the lab/OOF says (cap 6: lab -0.00057 -> public 0.956), so 'tiny OOF' no longer implies 'tiny public'. (2) Round 22 (B) finds that the largest missed pool is CLAIMED daughters (32/99), and our DaughterNet ranks only 3/35 of them. MITO3 is built for that pool: its features include d*_is_theft, q_inc, margins and the 'continuity alternative', and its edit undoes the theft. (3) The CI precedent shows that CC0 post-CSV stages from 0.96x teams were built and submitted under the aggressive-mode directive, though that is explicitly 'not a precedent'. RE-READ OF THE ARTIFACT: ker13_mito3_stage_v2.py plus mito3_ship.py form a post-CSV, edges-only stage. It asserts that the node set is unchanged, never raises and prints MITO3_DISARMED on any exception. It needs only the test zarr and the LightGBM booster s1_NK_ship89_plus_collision_deployed.txt (+ .names.json). Both are in the public CC0 dataset corwin1979/biocel-aux-4d9e2c17 (listed 01:1xZ: 520,226 B and 1,602 B). The ship call passes no probmat and no MITOSE head. The MITOSE checkpoints belong to biocel-data's pil_price_fork ILP pricing, a different component. The +0.00063 is a '199-film out-of-fold plate, sealed judge' number (44b6 +0, 6bba +0.00075; division TP 59->61, FP 68->70, priced precision 0.50), so it is out-of-fold, not in-sample. NEW VERDICT: the recorded reasons are PARTLY WRONG (it is pluggable, and the evidence is OOF), but the closure for 28-29 Sep STANDS. Reasons: new code after R8 without a new user OK; no honest lab (the DEPLOYED booster is presumably fit on all train films, so the exp60 lab would be in-sample, the edge-filter pattern); unmeasured runtime (image patches for every node of every film; test (D) is off because it took 55% of the runtime) on top of K2's 7.4-7.8 h, and it cannot share a file with CI's ~2 h; top-k = 1 edit per film, so ~2 TP / 2 FP of net fork change on 199 films; overlap with our insertion pool; lightgbm is not installed locally, so it was not measured. It goes to the post-deadline list as the first division-ADD item: a ready-made theft-aware ranker to benchmark against DaughterNet on the claimed pool.
